proof_attempt_summary: Derived matched original-record ATE absolute-risk and honest connected-length orders max(n^(-1/2), n^(-4alpha/(4alpha+1))), with root-n known-propensity comparators, no logarithmic loss, and an alpha=1/4 elbow. The characteristic-phase, guarded projection, localized finite-frequency reconstruction, and full-record converse proof spine passed fresh typed and math reviews after source attestation and prose synchronization. The field novelty forecast fell to subfield because of exact shared-translation scope, established methodological ancestry, and practically uninformative conservative intervals; stopped before Lean formalization under the standing below-floor decision.
tldr: For the ordinary heterogeneous mean ATE on the project-defined common conditional error model, original-record minimax absolute risk and honest connected-interval length both have the matched order \(n^{-\min\{1/2,4\alpha/(4\alpha+1)\}}\) with unknown propensity. Supplying only the true propensity on the same records gives order \(n^{-1/2}\) for both criteria. The elbow is exactly \(\alpha=1/4\); there is no logarithmic loss, and all four orders are independent of \(\nu\in[5/4,2]\). Explicit total procedures have public risk certificates and connected intervals with uniform coverage at least \(0.90\) for every finite \(n\ge2\), with full-range fallback for small samples. Matching converses retain complete outcome records and cover randomized procedures. Arbitrary common Borel noise, nonconstant Hölder locations and rough observational selection are retained. This class is non-nested with the randomized regular marginal-shift model of Athey et al. and the structured regular arm-error model of Kim v3; neither anchor theorem transfers and no strict class dominance is claimed.
